lines.text: On October 21, Meta said owners get one Class C share per share.
lines.say: On October twenty-first, Meta said owners get one Class C share per share.

lines.text: It's like a 2-for-1 split, but Class C can't vote. Meta says Zuckerberg keeps control.
lines.say: It's like a two-for-one split, but Class C can't vote. Meta says Zuckerberg keeps control.

lines.text: Meta says it could help raise capital. In Q3 2026 it spent $34.9B, while operations brought in $32.8B.
lines.say: Meta says it could help raise capital. In the third quarter, it spent thirty-four point nine billion dollars, while operations brought in thirty-two point eight.

lines.text: So free cash flow hit -$2.12 billion.
lines.say: So free cash flow hit negative two point one two billion.

lines.text: Sales rose 26%, but a $9.89B charge for a teen mental health settlement cut operating profit.
lines.say: Sales rose twenty-six percent, but a nine point eight nine billion dollar charge for a teen mental health settlement cut operating profit.

lines.text: Meta's stock fell sharply Thursday, down about 6% by midday.
lines.say: Meta's stock fell sharply Thursday, down about six percent by midday.

lines.text: Own an S&P 500 index fund? You likely own a slice of Meta.
lines.say: Own an S and P five hundred index fund? You likely own a slice of Meta.

lines.text: Watch January 19, 2027, when the change takes effect.

Meta's new shares come with zero votes.
Meta will give shareholders 1 nonvoting Class C share per share they own, set to take effect Jan 19, 2027.
Q3 2026: $34.9B capital spending vs $32.8B cash from operations, free cash flow -$2.12B.
Revenue +26% to $64.6B; a $9.89B teen-safety settlement charge (52 attorneys general) cut operating profit 37%. Stock fell sharply Thursday, about 6% by midday.
Sources: Meta Q3 2026 release (SEC 8-K), CNBC, Yahoo Finance.
